pages.summary: An image shown, with square pixels and no axes.
body: A gray image is shown through a gray colormap, from 0 (black) to 1 (white) for doubles, over the class's range for integers, or over [low high] (`[]` for the image's own range); a logical image in black and white; an m-by-n-by-3 array as colours; an indexed image with its colormap in those colours. With a spatial reference (`imref2d`) the image lies where it says, and the axes are shown in world coordinates.
syntax: An indexed image in its colours.

examples.title: Three kinds of image
In world units, and over a range

pages.summary: Images converted between classes, their ranges mapped.
body: Each maps the class's range onto the other's: integers to 0 to 1 for `im2double` and `im2single` (uint8 divided by 255, int16 shifted first), and 0 to 1 onto 0 to 255, 0 to 65535 or -32768 to 32767 for the integer ones (clipped and rounded). Logical images become 0 and 1. `'indexed'` converts colour indices, which count from 0 in integer classes and from 1 in floating ones.

examples.title: The same gray levels in five classes
examples.code:
I = [0 0.25 0.5 1];
u8 = im2uint8(I)
im2uint16(u8)
im2int16(I)
im2double(u8)
class(im2single(u8))
im2double(uint8([0 1 2]), 'indexed')
examples.output:
u8 =

  1×4 uint8 row vector

     0    64   128   255

ans =

  1×4 uint16 row vector

       0   16448   32896   65535

ans =

  1×4 int16 row vector

   -32768   -16384        0    32767

ans =

         0    0.2510    0.5020    1.0000

ans =

    'single'

ans =

     1     2     3

pages.summary: Images and colormaps made gray, and a matrix scaled to a gray image.
body: `rgb2gray` gives each pixel's luma, 0.2989 R + 0.5870 G + 0.1140 B, in the class of the image; for a colormap, a colormap of the gray levels. `im2gray` does the same for an RGB image and leaves a gray image as it is; `cmap2gray` makes a colormap gray. `mat2gray` scales any matrix to 0 to 1, its least value (or amin) to 0 and its largest (or amax) to 1.

examples.title: Colours and their gray levels
examples.code:
rgb = cat(3, [1 0 0], [0 1 0], [0 0 1]);
squeeze(rgb2gray(rgb))'
round(cmap2gray(parula(3)), 3)
mat2gray([10 20 40])
mat2gray([10 20 40], [0 50])

pages.summary: Colours as hue, saturation and value, and back; and their lightness.
body: Hue goes round the colour circle from 0 (red) through yellow (1/6), green (1/3), cyan (1/2), blue (2/3) and magenta (5/6) back to 1; saturation from 0 (gray) to 1 (pure); value from 0 (black) to 1 (brightest). Images (m-by-n-by-3) and colormaps (c-by-3) are both taken; integers are scaled to 0 to 1 first. `rgb2lightness` gives the perceived lightness L*, 0 for black to 100 for white.

examples.title: A colour wheel's hues, and a colour made paler
examples.code:
hsv = rgb2hsv([1 0 0; 1 1 0; 0 1 0; 0 0 1])
p = hsv2rgb([2/3 0.4 1])
round(rgb2lightness([0 0 1; 1 1 0; 0.5 0.5 0.5]), 1)
[h, s] = meshgrid(linspace(0, 1, 120), linspace(0, 1, 40));
imshow(hsv2rgb(cat(3, h, s, ones(40, 120))))

pages.summary: Indexed images: colour indices into a colormap, to and from RGB and gray images.
body: An indexed image holds indices into a colormap, counting from 1 in floating classes and from 0 in integer ones. `ind2rgb` gives the colours (as double), `ind2gray` the gray level of each colour. `gray2ind` makes a gray image indexed with n gray levels (64); `rgb2ind` chooses at most n colours (by minimum variance quantization), or a colour grid by a tolerance, or the colours of a given map, dithering unless `'nodither'` so that areas keep their average colour.

examples.title: Four colours, there and back
A gradient in eight colours, with and without dithering

pages.summary: The channels of an image, each as an array of its own.
body: For an RGB image the red, green and blue planes; for any image of k planes along the third dimension, k outputs.

pages.summary: Colour spaces: CIE L*a*b* and XYZ, and Y'CbCr.
body: `rgb2xyz` converts sRGB (or Adobe RGB, or linear RGB) to CIE 1931 XYZ, white's Y being 1; `rgb2lab` goes on to L*a*b*, where L* is lightness (0 to 100), a* runs from green to red and b* from blue to yellow, and equal distances are roughly equal differences to the eye; the white point is D65 unless named. `rgb2ycbcr` gives the ITU-R BT.601 luma and colour differences (Y from 16 to 235, Cb and Cr from 16 to 240, over 255 for doubles). Each has its inverse; the inverses keep out-of-gamut values in doubles and clip in other output types.

examples.title: White, red and a gray in three spaces
examples.code:
c = [1 1 1; 1 0 0; 0.5 0.5 0.5];
round(rgb2lab(c), 2)
round(rgb2xyz(c), 4)
round(255*rgb2ycbcr(c))
max(abs(lab2rgb(rgb2lab(c)) - c), [], 'all') < 1e-10

examples.title: Equal steps in RGB, unequal to the eye
examples.intro: The same step of 0.05 in one channel: in L*a*b* the step in the green is half again as large as the step in the purple.
